transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Sethi (ML Eng - Stratigo), Omar Haddad (Product), Claire Ngo (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick run through of weekly scorecard, focused defect triage on false positives coming from the summarization workflow, discussed latency regression after switching to a 13B variant and potential quick fixes.

[00:00] Lena: All right, everyone, thanks for joining. We lost a minute or two there but we should be good. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya: Hey, Priya here. Omar's on. Claire's on in the back.
[00:12] Omar: Yep, hi all.
[00:14] Marco: Marco Ruiz, Redwood SE. I'll jump into the bench numbers in a sec.
[00:18] Claire: Claire, security.
[00:20] Lena: Cool. High level agenda: one, go over the scorecard drift you flagged; two, guardrail false positives; three, latency / quantization options; four, action items. Sound good?
[00:28] Priya: Yep.
[00:30] Lena: Ok Marco, can you kick us off with the recent evals?
[00:34] Marco: Sure, real quick. So we've got the weekly scorecard — overall accuracy has dropped 3.8 points on the extractive QA set, most of that concentrated on long-context items. The boolean filter is flagging more false positives in the sanitation step — those are the guardrails that block shipments when we detect a risky phrase. The interesting part is the change lines up with the model switch last Friday to the 13B variant to reduce cost. It's, uh, a little noisier on longer prompts.
[00:56] Priya: Mm hm. We saw that in production, a bunch of returns where the answer was basically correct but the guardrail flagged it because of fuzzy match to our list.
[01:06] Omar: The business impact is that ops is getting tickets — we had 18 escalations yesterday — so we need that down.
[01:12] Lena: Understood. Do you have sample prompts?
[01:15] Priya: Yes, I'm going to share top failing 500 after this. Some are truncation issues. Some are just the model hallucinating a phrase that triggers the detector.
[01:24] Marco: Two quick axes to explore: prompt-set pruning (we remove templates that cause the model to produce those phrases) and guardrail tuning (loosen match thresholds for specific categories). We can run a guarded prune without touching production.
[01:36] Claire: Before we tune, we need to know retention of logs and ability to audit decisions. If you change guardrails, compliance needs a paper trail.
[01:44] Lena: Yes, Claire that's fair. We'll include audit logs and versioned rule changes in the rollout plan. Redwood Console keeps per-request tracing and model version tags — I can point you to that.
[01:54] Claire: The console screenshot I saw last week was helpful but I need specifics: how long are logs retained, are they stored in our K M S-encrypted bucket, and can we push them to our SIEM?
[02:04] Marco: Logs can be forwarded to your S3 in an encrypted stream, and you can bring your K M S keys for the private deployment. For hosted we support log forwarding with SSE-KMS. We'll get you the diagram.
[02:16] Claire: Great. That will help.
[02:18] Omar: On the latency front, the team says the 13B is longer tail latency for 95th percentile. How bad is it?
[02:26] Marco: Our bench: baseline with the 7B quantized cp profile — 95P ~ 240ms for 512 tokens. On 13B non-quantized it's 430ms 95P. If we run a 13B with INT8-ish quant profile we see ~310-330ms but quality slightly improves vs 7B. There's cost tradeoff.
[02:46] Priya: Does Redwood have continuous batching or is that something we manage?
[02:50] Lena: The runtime does continuous batching; you can set latency SLOs and batching aggressiveness in the route config. That helps average cost down. But the tail still matters for UX.
[02:59] Priya: Ok. For our UI we want sub-350ms 95P ideally for synchronous flows. Can we get that with 13B quant?
[03:06] Marco: Probably, but depends on token lengths. We suggested a small benchmark — 4k prompt subset with representative lengths. We'll run two quant profiles and the non-quant 13B to give you a matrix of latency vs cost vs score.
[03:20] Omar: That sounds like the next step.
[03:22] Lena: Priya, you mentioned truncation — are you chunking before the model call?
[03:27] Priya: We pre-chunk into 1k windows for the summarizer, but some prompts still hit 2k when users paste long notes. So some truncation behavior differs between 7B and 13B.
[03:36] Marco: That's useful. We'll include sequence-length distribution in the benchmark output.
[03:41] Claire: Back to security: if we do a Dedicated / private deployment, what's the install model? Do you ship an appliance or do we run an image in our V P C?
[03:50] Lena: For private we have two options — a V P C deployment where the control plane is customer-managed but we still orchestrate, or an on-prem bundle — appliance-style — for air-gapped environments. We'll share the private deployment checklist.
[04:03] Claire: Also need to confirm role-based access, S S O integration, and audit log retention policy.
[04:09] Lena: Yes we'll include SAML/SCIM docs and RBAC examples.
[04:13] Omar: Are there any quick fixes for the false positives we can deploy in the next 48 hours?
[04:18] Marco: Short-term: add a post-check with a secondary fuzzy matcher tuned to be more conservative before triggering a block. Longer-term: prompt surgery and model profile change. Short-term is low-risk.
[04:29] Priya: That would stop the ticket noise for ops.
[04:31] Lena: Good. Marco will run bench and propose the post-check thresholds.
[04:36] Marco: Yep. I'll also produce a list of candidate templates to prune.
[04:40] Priya: Quick nit — the guardrail false positives show different patterns by region. Could it be language tokenization?
[04:47] Marco: Possibly. We saw slight differences around unicode punctuation and common name variations. We'll add a tokenization normalization step in the staging pipeline.
[04:56] Omar: Any mention of competitors in your testing? Ops wants to know if we considered Anthropic or OpenAI for this workload.
[05:03] Lena: We've benchmarked broadly; we can share relative numbers but note differences in cost / licensing. I'll include a short competitor note.
[05:10] Claire: Also curious about auditability of model rollbacks. If you roll back a model version, can we see request traces and the model used?
[05:18] Marco: Yes, per-request model version tags and KV cache IDs are included in the trace. We keep immutable traces for the retention window you set.
[05:27] Priya: Great.
[05:29] Lena: Let's do a quick run through of the action items and owners. Marco will run the 4k benchmark, include latency/cost/score columns, and test two quant profiles. Priya will share failing prompts. Claire will send security checklist. I will share SOC2/ISO docs and K M S notes.
[05:45] Omar: Can we get the benchmark by Wednesday?
[05:47] Marco: Yes — I'll target Wednesday EOD, assuming we get the prompt subset today.
[05:53] Priya: I'll drop the top 500 now and follow up with the 4k subset by end of day.
[05:59] Claire: I'll get the V P C/security list by Monday.
[06:03] Lena: One more item — can we run a short canary on Dedicated for the top 10% traffic slice after benchmarks? This would let you validate in-production behavior without full migration.
[06:12] Marco: We can do a canary route with fallback to hosted. We'll include a rollout playbook.
[06:18] Omar: Sounds good.
[06:20] Lena: Ok, wrap up — we'll share artifacts in the drive: benchmark plan (Marco), SOC2 and K M S notes (Lena), failing prompts (Priya), and V P C checklist (Claire). Next meeting: security sync Thursday to finalize on-prem feasibility.
[06:33] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[06:34] Marco: Thanks.
[06:35] Lena: Thanks, bye.
